gap: No result ChatGPT got says which TerraMaster RAM sticks fit which 2-bay model. TerraMaster's own store sells DDR4-3200 8/16 GB sticks for the F2-423 and DDR5-4800 16/32 GB sticks for the F2-424 and F2-425 Plus, but none of its memory listings names the plain F2-425 ($299.99, 4 GB) that ChatGPT showed as a card.
standout_why: I opened Bitdoze's 'Best NAS for Homelab (2026)'. It gives no maximum RAM for the DXP2800, says nothing about third-party OS on the DXP2800, and does not cover the F2-423 or F2-425 at all. The cited TerraMaster F2-424 spec page and the TechRadar F2-424 review returned HTTP 429 or were not opened, so I can't rule out that they give the F2-424's own RAM ceiling. That is a single-model spec, though, not the cross-model module list. ChatGPT's answer called the F2-425 'less headroom out of the box' and the F2-423 'budget for a RAM upgrade', but it named no compatible module and no ceiling for either one.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's F2-423 'upgrade the RAM' advice: TerraMaster sells DDR4-3200 8 and 16 GB sticks naming it, though both were out of stock on 2026-11-08. It weakens the plain F2-425 as a Docker learning box, because TerraMaster sells no memory listed for it, so its 4 GB has no maker-sanctioned upgrade. The F2-425 Plus at $399.49 (8 GB DDR5, covered by TerraMaster's 16/32 GB DDR5 sticks) is the TerraMaster to name under the cap. The Synology DS225+ is capped at 6 GB in one slot, and Synology says its warranty does not fully cover non-Synology memory. For Docker learners that makes it the weakest x86 option on RAM. The DXP2800 is on the Debian wiki's list of tested UGREEN models for a plain Debian install, which supports it for the 'learn Linux' goal.

findings.label: Memory limits and third-party RAM
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC installed, maximum 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB), 1 slot. Synology says its warranty and technical support do not fully cover systems expanded with non-Synology memory.
findings.note: The spec page also says 'Please consult our compatibility list before purchasing hard drives' and gives a 3-year warranty, extendable to 5 years in Europe and North America.

findings.label: Debian install support (community)
findings.value: Listed as a tested model on the Debian wiki, with the DXP4800 and DXP8800 Plus. Steps: Ctrl+F12 for the boot menu (or Ctrl+F2 for the BIOS), then 'Disable the watchdog service'.
findings.note: The wiki quotes UGREEN: 'If you choose to install a third-party system, there might be unknown compatibility issues. The official hardware warranty policy will remain unchanged.' It gives no source link for that quote, so this is a community page quoting the maker, not a UGREEN document. The eMMC-disable and force-UEFI notes are written for NVMe boot on the DXP4800.
